question.text: `Grameen Urja Pvt Ltd`, a Section 8 company supplying off-grid solar to rural households in Jharkhand, approaches Mr. Arjun Desai (SIA) for its SE eligibility assessment. Under SEBI (ICDR) Reg 292B, what is the minimum proportion of activities/target population that must be directed toward the 16 eligible activities for an FPE to qualify as a Social Enterprise?

answer.text: 51% of activities or 51% of target population
67% of activities or 67% of target population (average of last 3 years)
85% of revenue, consistent with Section 11 of Income Tax Act

explanation.text: The Logic: Reg 292B(2) requires a For-Profit Enterprise (FPE) to demonstrate that at least 67% of its immediately preceding 3-year average of activities, revenue, expenditure, or target population is directed toward one or more of the 16 eligible activities listed in Reg 292B(1). The Trap: 51% is a simple-majority control threshold (Companies Act) and not the SE threshold. 75% and 85% are distractors that echo other regulatory thresholds (85% is the Section 11 Income Tax application rule, not SE eligibility). Cross-Exam Context: X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser) may be asked about CSR-eligible activities under Schedule VII; XXIII tests the SSE 67% threshold specifically. XIX-A/B/C/D/E references SVF (Cat I AIF) investing in FPEs — eligibility is tested at the SE level, not the fund level. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When evaluating a borderline FPE, compute the 67% test across all four metrics (activities, revenue, expenditure, beneficiaries) separately and document which metric was chosen. If revenue fails but beneficiaries pass, the SE still qualifies — but your working paper must spell out the basis clearly in case SEBI reviews the listing prospectus.
